isatvon_definition.i_instructions: Triggered by the Dify DMR's POST /tool/execute for skill_index 6 of Standard_BOM_Flow, after enrich_costing_sheet. Action: require cbom_db.cbom rows to already exist (hard ValueError otherwise); auto-resolve every cbom row where exactly one source (_costing/_erp/_qw) has data directly into cbom.duckdb's final_* columns, then persist genuine multi-source conflicts to Postgres logic_db.final_selection_conflicts for human review. Check: the DuckDB portion commits/rolls back as one transaction; the Postgres write (ensure_conflicts_table + idempotent DELETE-then-INSERT of unresolved conflicts) happens inside its own explicit BEGIN/COMMIT in run_resolve_final_selection. Bound: single attempt, no retry loop. Business rule: this tool ALWAYS returns hitl:1, even when there are zero pending conflicts -- it is the platform's only gate before Finalize Price / CBOM preview, so it must never be silently skipped; hitl_router.py's own submit endpoint accepts an empty resolutions list as a no-op confirm precisely to handle the zero-conflict case.

fresh_state_parameters: cbom_db.cbom rows for this rfq_id -- REQUIRED precondition; raises ValueError otherwise
cbom rows' _costing/_erp/_qw source columns (which of the 3 have non-null data determines auto-resolve vs conflict)
Pre-existing UNRESOLVED rows in logic_db.final_selection_conflicts for this rfq_id (resolved_source IS NULL) -- deleted and replaced on every re-run; already-resolved rows are never touched

a_automation.action_step: BEGIN TRANSACTION (DuckDB); run the auto-resolve SQL for single-source rows and recompute derived columns; query genuine multi-source conflicts; COMMIT. Then, in a separate Postgres transaction: ensure_conflicts_table(pg_conn) (idempotent DDL/migration), DELETE this rfq_id's unresolved conflicts, INSERT the current conflict set, COMMIT.
a_automation.acceptance_check: No exception raised in either the DuckDB or Postgres transaction. The response always reports hitl:1 -- this is a fixed business rule, not conditioned on the acceptance check's outcome.

t_tech_stack.action_tool: resolve_final_selection (this tool itself, delegating to reporting_pipeline.run_resolve_final_selection -> final_selection.resolve_final_selection, which also writes Postgres logic_db.final_selection_conflicts)
t_tech_stack.fixed_check_tool: None -- no independent validation MCP tool exists. Human review of the actual conflicts happens through a SEPARATE service, hitl_router.py (port 5002/5102), but that is a review/resolution UI backend, not a validation-check tool for THIS tool's own execution.

v_variables.success_gate: resolve_final_selection() completes without raising in both the DuckDB and Postgres transactions
v_variables.no_op_condition: None in the DuckDB auto-resolve step (always re-evaluates every cbom row); the Postgres side IS idempotent in a specific way -- re-running deletes and replaces only UNRESOLVED conflicts, never touching already-resolved ones, so a repeat call safely refreshes the pending set without discarding completed human review
v_variables.escalation_condition: hitl:1 is returned UNCONDITIONALLY on every successful call, even with pending_conflicts==0 -- the caller (fastapi_router.py) will never advance rfq_process_stage past this skill on its own; hitl_router.py's POST /api/rfq/{rfq_id}/final-selection is what actually clears the way, and only once every conflict is resolved
v_variables.budget_limit: 300s MCP Jungle call_tool() timeout / 600s Dify HTTP node timeout

o_outcome.state_handoff_file: The one tool of these 10 with a genuine, real append-style state artifact: logic_db.final_selection_conflicts (Postgres) -- created/migrated idempotently by ensure_conflicts_table(), holding conflict_id/rfq_id/cbom_item_id/bom_item_id/volume_no/cpn/available_sources/resolved_source/resolved_by/resolved_at/created_at. This is the closest real analog in this platform to ISATVON's 'mandatory audit trail artifact', though it is a live working-state table (rows get UPDATEd on resolution) rather than a strictly append-only log.

ui_updates: Generic {skillCode:'M03.6_FinalSelectionHITL', skillName:'Resolve Final Cost Selection (HITL gate)', stepStatus} pushed via fastapi_router.py's notify_skill_progress()

Dify's DMR additionally calls the accomplish-ui daemon's POST /api/internal/trigger-hitl ({rfqId, stage:'centum_reporting__resolve_final_selection', hitlType:'approval'}) specifically because hitl==1, broadcasting a hitl:request SSE event that opens the frontend's pricing-source-review UI
database_updates: file_metadata_db.rfq_process_tracking.hitl_required set true by fastapi_router.py (since hitl is always truthy here)
logic_db.final_selection_conflicts rows inserted/cleared as described above
cbom_db.cbom's final_* columns updated for every auto-resolved (single-source) row
alerts: None beyond the SSE hitl:request event -- no separate paging/escalation channel confirmed

orchestration.trigger: HTTP_POST_Payload_plus_Variables (POST /tool/execute); Dify additionally calls the daemon directly on hitl==1

persistence.database: DuckDB (cbom.duckdb, read+write) AND PostgreSQL logic_db -- the only one of these 10 tools that writes to Postgres directly rather than only DuckDB
persistence.action: Two separate transactions: DuckDB BEGIN/COMMIT for auto-resolve, then a Postgres BEGIN/COMMIT for the conflicts table -- not one atomic cross-database transaction

audit.telemetry: logic_db.final_selection_conflicts itself functions as the real audit surface for this tool, plus a single logging_utils.logger info-level line

ui.method: SSE push via rfq:skill-progress AND a dedicated hitl:request event (via the daemon's POST /api/internal/trigger-hitl), since this tool always halts the pipeline
